columns.printed: Smallest k reaching the comparator's accuracy

interval.printed: gaps d and the cached view: paired BCa bootstrap over puzzles, 95%, B = 10,000 (the same for the locked tests, free analysis 3 and free analysis 12); break-even: cluster bootstrap over puzzles, 95%, 2,000 draws for the Haiku-max rows (free analysis 12); Study 1's pre-specified Haiku-medium break-even rows: the same kind of interval from the locked analysis, whose draw count is not stamped

n.printed: Study 1: 80 puzzles per test, in the test's shape; the Haiku-medium vote draws its k from 40 samples per puzzle, and the comparator gives 1 sample per puzzle; Study 1's pre-specified Haiku-medium break-even uses the same puzzles per shape. Study 1b: Test B2 and Test B1 on 80 puzzles at 16 steps, each puzzle's chain and pieces pooled; the Haiku-max break-even on 40 puzzles at 6 steps and 80 at 12 steps and 16 steps. In Study 1b the Haiku-max vote draws its k from 10 samples per puzzle and shape at every length, and Opus-medium's samples per puzzle and shape (2, 1 and 2 on the 6-step, 12-step and 16-step sets) are averaged

price.printed: list prices of the pinned table, re-scaled per row

set.printed: Study 1: the main-run puzzle set at 6 steps; Study 1b: the 16-step set for Tests B1 and B2, and the 6-step, 12-step and 16-step sets for the Haiku-max break-even

notes.printed: The stamped label of free analysis 12 reads

notes.raw: post hoc sensitivity: how far the equal-money readings rest on one price list; no reading

notes.printed: Samples per comparator answer: the comparator's cost per answer divided by the cost of one Haiku sample (at the price ratio in the row; in Panel 1, at list price).
The price ratio is per token, comparator over Haiku, the same for input and output (the pinned table's is
for Sonnet); token counts are held as measured. At the list ratio each row is the locked test and prints its d and interval.

One comparison, one interval: any other re-priced row that is the same comparison as a printed result (the same settings, k and puzzle set) takes that result and its label, named in the last column. A Test 1 row held at the locked test's k is Test 1 as run; Test B2's one-sample vote is Test B1 (one Haiku-max sample against Opus-medium on the same 16-step set); its votes at other k are free analysis 3's rows at that k. The remaining rows are post hoc (free analysis 12), with no reading.
Held: the cost-matched k at that price exceeds the samples drawn per puzzle and shape, so k is held at that number.

Accuracies in the main panel are given to two decimals, as the tests' own tables give them, so a row that is a locked test prints the same numbers; d always has two. d is the difference of the unrounded accuracies, so it can differ in its last digit from the difference of the two printed accuracies.

Under the original pre-registered marking rule, which Deviation 2 kept as a sensitivity check, Test 3 would read inconclusive instead of worse by more than the margin (d = +0.30 points, 95% interval −13.58 to +14.95).
raw: worse by more than the margin

notes.printed: A break-even interval end is "unbounded" when too many replicates never reach the comparator's accuracy within the samples drawn; the share of such replicates is shown.

Break-even intervals (Panel 1): the Haiku-max rows' cluster bootstrap uses 2,000 draws (free analysis 12); the Haiku-medium rows are Study 1's pre-specified break-even (item 9d), whose interval comes from the locked analysis, and the locked file does not stamp its number of draws, so none is given here.
